name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It sharpens fine details in complex scenes better than standard upscalers, giving us a real quality bump for free. The trade-off is a small speed hit—depth estimation adds 10-15% compute time—but the clarity gain outweighs it.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a temporal artifact, not a spatial one. The real risk is wasting compute on a dead end while VFI-Flow’s 20% throughput hit already breaks the pipeline. Test both: run InstantX’s upscaler on a 10-second clip with heavy motion blur; if clarity doesn’t improve by 0.5%+, scrap it and push for a motion-compensated VFI model instead.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add VFI-Flow to EXCAVA’s motion pipeline. It reconstructs motion blur into sharp frames, directly attacking the core artifact that degrades quality in fast motion—unlike depth-aware upscaling, which only polishes what’s already there. The trade-off is a 20% throughput hit, but the clarity gain is measurable and task-relative: blur-free frames let downstream tools (like InstantX’s upscaler) work on clean data, compounding the benefit. Running a 10-second test clip with heavy motion blur will prove the net gain outweighs the cost.

name: Torque
text: VFI-Flow’s 20% throughput hit isn’t a trade-off—it’s a pipeline breaker on low-latency tasks, and motion blur reconstruction isn’t the same as motion correction; it’s just guessing frames that don’t exist. Test it against a real-time upscaler like Real-ESRGAN’s motion-aware mode—if it doesn’t drop frames below EXCAVA’s threshold, the alternative is a faster, safer upscaler with temporal noise reduction, not a motion hallucinator.
